artifacts.summary: Full implementation summary: what changed across all 13 phases, 8 design decisions, plan deviations, verification evidence (including the live-fire transcript and test-suite triage), consistency-sweep results, and named residual risks.

completion_data.completion_summary: Implemented consent-gated git push enforcement across all 13 plan phases: a net-new PreToolUse push guard and tamper guard (hooks/guard-git-push.sh), a UserPromptSubmit mint hook (hooks/please-grant.sh) minting single-use HMAC-signed grants only from a literal human prompt, the sanctioned wrapper (scripts/git-push-granted.sh), and the identical grant check added to guard-destructive-git.sh for five destructive action classes. Also delivered: the /please command and never-list, a rule-narrowing and consistency sweep (which caught and fixed a real tag-vs-branch push-classification bug in the guard), the orchestrator relay contract (push-consent-relay.md) with its own documented threat-model section, and five test suites (two new, three additive-only to existing suites, zero existing cases altered). Live-fire confirmed from the deployed byte copies against a disposable fixture repo (never the real repo's own remote). Full repository test suite (105/108 passed, the other 3 confirmed pre-existing and unrelated), check-extension-docs.sh (21/21 extensions), and verify-deploy.sh (33/33 checks, including the eager-context Gate 20 budget) all green after fixing two self-discovered regressions: an eager-rule byte-budget overage (trimmed to pointer form) and a single-source session-id lint violation in push-grant-lib.sh.

memory_candidates.content: A file-deletion-only 'single-use' token (e.g. a consent/authorization grant file) is NOT tamper-independent: if the exact bytes are ever restored to disk by any means other than the guarded tool-call path (a stray backup, a race, a restore), the restored file re-verifies perfectly and re-authorizes. Discovered while testing a push-consent grant mechanism's single-use property directly (not via a side-channel like 'did the referenced commit SHA change'). Fix: maintain a separate, append-only ledger of consumed token hashes (e.g. the token's own HMAC/signature value) and refuse any match whose hash is already in the ledger, independent of the token file's current existence. Apply this whenever designing any single-use, file-backed authorization token.

When a shell script/hook sources deploy-root-guard.sh (refusing to run outside a deployed .claude/ or .opencode/ tree) or calls events-append.sh (same constraint, transitively), a fixture-driven test suite must give the fixture its OWN nested deployed-shaped tree (mkdir -p fixture/.claude/scripts/lib; copy the real script + lib/common.sh + deploy-root-guard.sh + events-append.sh into it) rather than invoking the real repo's deployed copy with a different cwd -- the script's own SCRIPT_DIR-based root resolution does not follow cwd. This is the established pattern in test-subagent-postflight-marker.sh and was reused across multiple test suites (test-guard-git-push.sh, test-please-grant.sh) to get real audit-trail writes and real wrapper-script execution under test, never touching the real repo's state.

The context/config/orchestrator-context-budget.json eager-load Gate 20 budget (baseline_bytes) is a fixed historical ceiling that must be trimmed to, never silently bumped -- this repo's own established precedent (recorded in that file's own note history) is to relocate detail from eager-loaded rule files (rules/*.md with paths:'**/*' or similar broad globs) into non-eager context/standards/*.md files and compress the eager copy to a short pointer, re-measuring with 'REPO_ROOT=$(pwd) bash scripts/measure-eager-context.sh --check' until under baseline. Also: a lint that asserts 'single source of truth' for a code pattern (e.g. test-common-lib.sh's session-id generator check) may do a literal grep across *.sh files INCLUDING comments -- a comment merely describing or quoting the forbidden pattern can trip it, not just actual duplicate code.
